title: KV preemption spiral at low load
summary: A fleet well inside its rated request rate, collapsing because contexts are what fill the cache and contexts are not requests.

steps.title: Two sessions a second, four replicas, and the cache fills inside a minute
body: The router is power-of-two-choices, so this is not an imbalance problem. The offered rate is well under rated capacity, so it is not a throughput problem either.

Per finding 8: at two sessions a second on four replicas, parked context fills a 30k-token cache inside a minute. Each of those conversations keeps its context resident between turns for as long as the user is reading, and a replica holding a few of those has no room left regardless of how few requests it is serving.
steps.look_for: KV utilization high while the queue depths stay small. Those two facts together are the whole dynamic.

steps.title: Take away a third of the cache: no eviction path
body: This run, kv-spiral-never, never swaps a preempted sequence to DRAM. It discards the sequence and pays to recompute the prefill later, about 270 ms for 4k tokens and proportionally more for 40k.
Preemption without an eviction tier is not capacity relief. It is capacity spent twice on the same request, with no cheaper path available.
steps.look_for: The preemption rate rising, and the discard-and-recompute path carrying all of it, because there is no DRAM tier in this run.

steps.title: Without eviction: 2% attainment, 36 s p99 TTFT
body: Per finding 8: without eviction, late attainment is 2% and p99 TTFT is 36 s. Throughput is not the problem the fleet is still producing tokens; almost none of them arrive inside their service objective, because every preempted sequence pays a stall its client can see.
Ranking this configuration on throughput would look fine. Ranking it on goodput would not, which is why goodput is the headline number.
steps.look_for: The two lines separating, and the wasted-GPU fraction in the Utilization tab climbing.

steps.title: Swap to DRAM at 50 GB/s and the same load holds
body: Open the A/B view with A = kv-spiral-never (this run) and B = kv-spiral-swap, DRAM at 50 GB/s, at the same offered load.

Per finding 8: swapping to DRAM at 50 GB/s serves the same load at 95% attainment, 84 ms p99 TTFT, 2.2 preemptions a second, 1,426 vs 780 tokens/s. The preemptions do not stop; the cost of each one drops enough that they stop mattering.
steps.look_for: Attainment and p99 TTFT separating sharply between A and B, while both keep preempting.

steps.title: The fix is a tiering decision, not a routing one
body: No routing policy recovers from a cache too small for the context lengths being offered, which is worth knowing before spending a quarter on a better router. What recovers it is giving preemption somewhere cheap to go.
1,426 vs 780 tokens/s at the same 95% vs 2% attainment is the DRAM swap path paying for itself: preemption stops being wasted work once discard-and-recompute is no longer the only option.
steps.look_for: Preemptions continuing at 2.2 a second in the swap run while attainment holds at 95%, with the routing policy unchanged.
